Growing a city garden

A city garden can provide fresh vegetables throughout the summer. Start with a sunny corner and deep containers that allow roots to spread. Good drainage keeps the plants healthy after heavy rain.

Water the soil early in the morning and add compost at the beginning of each season. Tomatoes and beans need strong supports, while lettuce grows well in smaller pots. Regular observation helps gardeners notice pests before they spread.

Share seeds with neighbours and record which varieties grow best in your local conditions. Over several seasons these notes become a useful guide to planting, harvesting, and making the most of a small outdoor space.
